edits.old:
### What is the average cost of a wedding photographer in Australia?

There is no single honest figure, because a national average blends very different weddings. Ask several photographers to quote against the same written brief and compare inclusions, not headline prices.
edits.new:
### Why don't you give an average cost for a wedding photographer?

Because a national average blends very different weddings, and a figure built from other people's days can't tell you what yours will cost. Send several photographers the same written brief, then use the comparison steps above to read their quotes side by side.

edits.old:
Under the [consumer guarantees](https://www.accc.gov.au/consumers/buying-products-and-services/consumer-rights-and-guarantees), service providers must carry out all services using an acceptable level of care and skill, and their work must be at least as good as what a competent service provider with average skills and experience would provide. <!-- fact_200 -->

Services, and any resulting products, must be [fit for any stated purpose](https://www.accc.gov.au/consumers/buying-products-and-services/consumer-rights-and-guarantees) when you tell the provider what you want the service for. <!-- fact_201 --> So say it plainly at booking: an album for your parents, prints for the hallway, a feature in a magazine.

Services must be [supplied within a reasonable time](https://www.accc.gov.au/consumers/buying-products-and-services/consumer-rights-and-guarantees) if there's no agreed time frame. <!-- fact_202 --> An agreed delivery date in the contract is clearer for everyone than "a reasonable time".

These [basic rights can't be taken away](https://www.accc.gov.au/consumers/buying-products-and-services/consumer-rights-and-guarantees) by anything a business says or does, including saying it isn't responsible for problems with a product or service. <!-- fact_203 -->

When a service has a [major problem](https://www.accc.gov.au/consumers/problem-with-a-product-or-service-you-bought/repair-replace-refund-cancel), you can choose to cancel the contract and get a refund, which may not be a full refund because you pay a reasonable amount for any work done so far and as expected, or keep the contract and pay a lower price that takes the problem into account. <!-- fact_204 -->

A change of heart is a different matter. You are not entitled to a repair, replacement or refund under the consumer guarantees if you got what you asked for but [simply changed your mind](https://www.accc.gov.au/consumers/problem-with-a-product-or-service-you-bought/repair-replace-refund-cancel), though a business with a change of mind policy must follow it. <!-- fact_205 -->

The [ACCC](https://www.accc.gov.au/consumers/buying-products-and-services/consumer-rights-and-guarantees) doesn't provide legal advice about what consumers are entitled to. <!-- fact_207 --> For a question about your own agreement, get advice on your own contract from a lawyer.
